figures.alt: Localized moisture-softened wood at the lower corner of an exterior door jamb
figures.caption: The lower jamb takes standing water and splashback. Probe the jamb, threshold, trim, and adjacent wall before deciding how much material must be replaced.
figures.before: When You Need a Permit in Jacksonville

figures.alt: Finished composite exterior trim with a sloped sill and narrow caulk joint
figures.caption: A durable repair has to return the opening to a straight, drainable exterior face. New trim and sealant cannot protect wood that remains wet behind the surface.

figures.alt: Roof runoff moving through a shallow swale away from a Florida foundation
figures.caption: If roof water or grade keeps wetting the opening, correct that water path as part of the repair. Otherwise a clean jamb splice can inherit the same failure.
